message.content:
**Hydrogen (H)** – the simplest and most abundant element in the universe.

| Property | Value / Description |
|----------|---------------------|
| **Atomic number** | 1 |
| **Symbol** | H |
| **Common isotope** | ^1H (protium) – 99.98 % natural abundance |
| **Other stable isotopes** | ^2H (deuterium, 0.02 %) and ^3H (tritium, radioactive, ~10⁻⁵ %) |
| **Atomic mass** | 1.00794 u (average weighted by natural isotopic composition) |
| **Electron configuration** | 1s¹ |
| **Valence electrons** | 1 |
| **Electronegativity (Pauling)** | 2.20 |
| **First ionization energy** | 13.598 eV (1312 kJ mol⁻¹) |
| **Second ionization energy** | 24.587 eV (2375 kJ mol⁻¹) |
| **Electron affinity** | –72.8 kJ mol⁻¹ (negative, meaning energy is released when an electron is added) |
| **Boiling point** | –252.87 °C (20.28 K) at 1 atm |
| **Melting point** | –259.16 °C (14.01 K) at 1 atm |
| **Density** | 0.08988 g L⁻¹ at 25 °C (very low; lighter than air) |
| **Molar volume** | 22.414 L mol⁻¹ (ideal gas at STP) |
| **State at room temperature** | Gas |
| **Bonding** | Forms covalent bonds; diatomic molecules (H₂) are the most common form. Can also form hydrides with metals or nonmetals. |
| **Reactivity** | Highly reactive; forms acids (e.g., HCl, H₂SO₄), bases (e.g., NaOH via water electrolysis), and many organic compounds. Combustion produces water vapor. |
| **Uses** | Fuel (hydrogen fuel cells), industrial feedstock (ammonia synthesis, petroleum refining), laboratory reagent, cryogenic coolant (liquid hydrogen). |
| **Safety notes** | Extremely flammable; forms explosive mixtures with air (1–4 % H₂ in air). Requires careful handling and proper ventilation. |

---

### Quick facts

* **Lightest element** – only one proton and one electron in its ground state.
* **Most abundant element** – makes up about 75 % of the visible baryonic matter in the universe.
* **Key role in stars** – nuclear fusion of hydrogen into helium powers the Sun and other stars.
* **Isotopic significance** – deuterium is used as a tracer in geochemistry and cosmology; tritium is a beta‑emitter used in nuclear weapons and radiolabeling studies.

Feel free to ask if you’d like more detail on any specific property!
